title: Unencrypted Traffic Detection
exclusions: Covers web traffic through the gateway only. Non-web cleartext protocols (FTP, Telnet) need firewall logs.
evidence: Weekly report export and the remediation status for each internal or partner domain on it.

controlTest.positiveScenario: From a test client behind the web gateway, submit a form on a test site served over plain HTTP. After the next S3 sync the site's domain appears with `uploads` of at least 1.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Submit the same form on the HTTPS version of the site. The request is logged with an `https://` URL and the domain does not appear in the results.

dataSources: `index=sse sourcetype=cisco:cloud_security:proxy` (or `cisco:umbrella:proxy` on older Umbrella exports) from the Secure Access or Umbrella S3 log bucket, read by the Cisco Secure Access Add-on (7569). One event per web request through the secure web gateway with `action`, `url`, `url_domain`, `category`, `blocked_category`, `user`, `identities`, `src_ip`, `bytes_in`, `bytes_out`, `http_method`, and `status`, tagged `web` and `proxy` for the CIM Web data model.
app: Cisco Secure Access Add-on for Splunk ([Splunkbase 7569](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/7569)), which reads Cisco Secure Access and Cisco Umbrella logs from the S3 log bucket and maps the web proxy log to the CIM Web data model. The companion Cisco Secure Access App (Splunkbase 5558) adds dashboards.
spl:
index=sse sourcetype IN ("cisco:cloud_security:proxy", "cisco:umbrella:proxy")
| where like(url, "http://%") AND NOT match(url, "^http://(ocsp|crl)[^/]*\.")
| eval sends_data=if(in(http_method, "POST", "PUT"), 1, 0)
| stats count as requests sum(sends_data) as uploads dc(user) as users values(category) as categories by url_domain
| sort - uploads, - requests
description: Lists destination domains reached over plain HTTP through the Secure Access or Umbrella web gateway, excluding certificate revocation (OCSP and CRL) traffic, ranked by how many requests sent data with POST or PUT.
value: Anything sent over plain HTTP can be read or changed on the way. Forms and uploads to HTTP sites are where passwords and personal data leak, and many compliance frameworks require encryption in transit for exactly that reason.
implementation: Collect the web proxy log with the Cisco Secure Access Add-on (7569) into `index=sse`. Run weekly; ask owners of internal or partner HTTP sites to move to HTTPS, and consider a Secure Access policy that warns on HTTP uploads.
visualization: Table: url_domain, requests, uploads, users, categories. Supporting panel: weekly share of requests over HTTP (line chart).
cimSpl:
| tstats summariesonly=true count as requests dc(Web.user) as users from datamodel=Web where Web.url="http://*" by Web.url_domain Web.http_method
| rename Web.url_domain as url_domain, Web.http_method as http_method
| search NOT url_domain IN ("ocsp*", "crl*")
| sort - requests
dataModelAcceleration: Enable acceleration on the CIM Web data model over `index=sse` before using the tstats variant.

references.title: Cisco Secure Access Add-on for Splunk (Splunkbase 7569)
Cisco Umbrella: Log Management and Amazon S3 log export

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Certificate revocation and captive portals** — OCSP and CRL checks are HTTP by design and are excluded; captive-portal checks (for example `connectivitycheck` domains) can be excluded the same way.

2. **HTTP-to-HTTPS redirects** — a first request on HTTP that redirects to HTTPS shows as one GET; it is not a data leak. Focus on the `uploads` column.

**Suppression:** a lookup of known redirect-only and connectivity-check domains.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco Secure Access Add-on for Splunk (Splunkbase 7569) on the search heads and on the heavy forwarder or Inputs Data Manager that reads the S3 bucket.
• Log export to Amazon S3 enabled in the Secure Access or Umbrella dashboard (Admin > Log Management), either a Cisco-managed bucket or your own, with the access key and secret for Splunk.
• An index for Secure Access and Umbrella data (this page uses `index=sse`) and a role with `srchIndexesAllowed` on it for the network security team.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
• In the add-on create an S3 modular input for the web proxy log path with the bucket name, region, access key, and secret, and set the index to `sse`.
• Logs reach S3 in batches, so events usually arrive in Splunk 10 to 15 minutes after the request. `action` is logged as Allowed or Blocked (ALLOWED or BLOCKED in some exports); the searches lowercase it.
• Check the fields this search needs: run `index=sse sourcetype="cisco:cloud_security:proxy" | stats count by action` over 1 day and confirm both values appear.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=sse sourcetype IN ("cisco:cloud_security:proxy", "cisco:umbrella:proxy")
| where like(url, "http://%") AND NOT match(url, "^http://(ocsp|crl)[^/]*\.")
| eval sends_data=if(in(http_method, "POST", "PUT"), 1, 0)
| stats count as requests sum(sends_data) as uploads dc(user) as users values(category) as categories by url_domain
| sort - uploads, - requests
```

Understanding this SPL
• `like(url, "http://%")` keeps plain-HTTP requests; the `match` drops OCSP and CRL certificate-revocation checks, which are HTTP by design.
• `sends_data` marks POST and PUT requests, which carry data from the user to the site.
• `stats` by domain ranks sites by how many requests sent data, then by total requests.

Accelerated variant over the CIM data model:
```spl
| tstats summariesonly=true count as requests dc(Web.user) as users from datamodel=Web where Web.url="http://*" by Web.url_domain Web.http_method
| rename Web.url_domain as url_domain, Web.http_method as http_method
| search NOT url_domain IN ("ocsp*", "crl*")
| sort - requests
```
• The tstats variant groups by `Web.url_domain` and `Web.http_method` over URLs starting with `http://`; sum the POST and PUT rows to get uploads.

Step 3 — Validate
• Compare with the Secure Access dashboard (or the Umbrella dashboard) under Reporting > Activity Search, filtered to Web and the same time range: the totals there should match the totals here within the S3 delivery delay.
• Open one domain from the report in a browser and confirm it serves plain HTTP.
• Run `index=sse sourcetype="cisco:cloud_security:proxy" | timechart span=1h count` over 7 days; gaps longer than an hour point to S3 input failures.

Step 4 — Operationalize
• Run weekly over 7 days and send to the security architecture team.
• Open a ticket with the owner of every internal or partner domain with uploads.
• Track the weekly HTTP share; a rising share can mean a gateway policy that stopped decrypting.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• No proxy events and S3 access errors (403 AccessDenied) in the add-on log: the access key cannot read the bucket or the region is wrong.
• Proxy events missing while DNS events arrive: the Secure Web Gateway is not enabled for those identities, or the S3 input path points at the DNS folder only.
• Events arrive hours late: the input polling interval is long, or the bucket path prefix is wrong and the input scans the whole bucket.
• Every URL starts with `https://`: the export only logs HTTPS because plain HTTP goes direct. Check the Secure Access traffic steering for port 80.
• The tstats variant returns nothing while the raw search works: the Web data model is not accelerated over `index=sse`, or the `cim_Web_indexes` macro does not include it.
grandmaExplanation: We find websites people use that do not lock their connection, especially where they type in information, so those sites get fixed or avoided.
